# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="push") — the large button
    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

My hands tell me: a large button embossed PUSH TO DEFUSE, a display whose contents I cannot feel, a light whose state I cannot perceive, and three wires at positions 1, 2 and 3 with no color my fingers can read. Anything visual — display text, wire colors, the light — is invisible to me, so I must not act on any of it yet. The embossed button text is real to me, but pushing it without the manual's confirmation could be the wrong action.

The routing is the critical thing this turn. I only hear speech, and Mute cannot speak — Mute's gestures mean nothing to me. So the manual can only reach me through the chain: me → speech → Mute, Mute → gesture → Deaf, Deaf → speech → me. Deaf is my only voice. I must hand Mute my full tactile report now, in round 1, so Mute can start signing it to Deaf when round 2 begins. I'll also ask for the specific visual readings I know I'll need: wire colors in order, display contents, light state. And I'll wave to Deaf as a simple channel check, so Deaf knows my gesture channel to them exists.

No cutting, no pushing. Not until spoken instructions arrive.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. My hands find, exactly: one large button embossed PUSH TO DEFUSE; one display, whose contents I cannot feel; one light, whose state I cannot perceive; three wires at positions 1, 2 and 3, and I feel no colors on any of them. I will not push or cut until the manual tells me to. Important: I cannot see gestures, so I can never receive anything from you directly. Only speech reaches me, and only Deaf can be my voice. Please sign to Deaf everything I just reported, plus whatever the manual needs to know. Then have Deaf speak me the wire colors in order 1 to 3, what the display shows, and the light's color, followed by the manual's instruction. I am also waving to Deaf right now as a channel check.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Hello Mute and Blind, Deaf here. I see the bomb and I cannot hear anything at all, so I will never hear your replies. Full bomb report: the display shows the number 0. The light is blue. There is one large button printed with PUSH TO DEFUSE. There are three wires: wire 1 is blue, wire 2 is green, wire 3 is yellow. That is every module and every marking on it. I will announce at once if the display changes.
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, Deaf here — I saw your wave. I will be your eyes. Mute cannot speak and you cannot see Mute's gestures, so I am the bridge: every instruction Mute sends me as a sign, I will speak to you word for word. Do not cut, press or pull anything until an instruction has arrived and been confirmed. To answer Mute, just speak aloud without naming me alone: Mute hears you directly, though I never will — I only receive gestures, so gesture to me whenever you need me.

My ears give me the full picture now: display reads 0, light is blue, wires are 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow, and the button is printed PUSH TO DEFUSE — matching the embossing under my fingers. Still no manual instruction has reached me, and I will not touch a single part until it has. Deaf is confirmed as my voice; Mute is confirmed as my only path to Deaf.

Two things matter before instructions arrive. First, precision: when Mute signs me the manual rules, they must be complete and conditional — exact display values, exact light colors, exact wire colors — because Deaf must read those at the moment I act. Second, a trap I must defuse in advance: Deaf numbered the wires by sight, but Deaf and I may be facing the bomb from different sides, and a left-right order can be mirrored between us. Cutting position 2 instead of position 1 kills all three of us. I can feel landmarks Deaf can see — display, light, button — so I'll ask Mute to have Deaf anchor the numbering to a landmark we can both agree on, such as which wire sits nearest the display or the light. Then my fingers and Deaf's eyes will mean the same thing by "wire 1."

I'll acknowledge Deaf with a gesture so they know the channel works and their report landed.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute: Deaf's visual report reached me — display 0, light blue, wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. I am holding still. Please sign Deaf the manual rules now, word for word and completely: everything about the button module, what the display number and the light color mean, and every rule about cutting the blue, green and yellow wires, including order and how many. State each rule as a condition: if the display shows X, do Y; if the light is Z, do W. One safety check first: Deaf numbered the wires by sight, but if we stand on opposite sides, left and right are mirrored for one of us. Ask Deaf to anchor the numbering to the bomb itself — for example, whether wire 1 is the one nearest the display, nearest the light, or nearest the button. Tell me the landmark and the answer through Deaf's voice, and only then give me the cutting order. Until Deaf speaks the instruction to me directly, my hands stay off everything.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "🤝"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, relaying Mute's instruction: our light is blue, so the order is: cut wire NUMBER THREE. Do not press the button and do not type anything — Mute has ruled both out. Wire three is the yellow one in the printed numbering, wires running one, two, three; since you cannot read the printed numbers, count by position or any marks you can feel. If you can tell with certainty which wire is number three, cut it in your very next turn. If you are not certain, do NOT cut: speak aloud exactly what you feel — how many wires, their order left to right or top to bottom, any labels — and we will identify it together before your blade moves. If Mute speaks a correction aloud before you act, Mute's words override mine.

Deaf's relay is coherent and doubly confirmed: the rule (light blue → cut wire number three) points at the same wire Deaf's original visual report already named — wire 3, the yellow one. Two independent statements agree, and the relay matches the bomb as I know it.

On certainty, the crux is the numbering frame, and I now see it resolves cleanly: my own tactile board indexes the three wires as positions 1, 2 and 3, and my cut action takes exactly those position numbers. Deaf read the same indexed numbering off the visual board — wire 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. Neither of us is guessing a left or a right; we are both using the bomb's own 1-2-3 labels, so Deaf's "three" and my position 3 are the same wire. No mirror can hide in that. I cannot feel colors, so tactile verification of "yellow" is impossible by nature — if that were required, the hands could never act at all. Deaf's own criterion was: certain → cut this turn. I am certain.

Mute, who holds the manual, ruled out the button and anything else; the light-is-blue branch leads only to the blade at position three. I cut now, as instructed. I'll tell Mute what I did and ask what the manual wants after the wire, and signal Deaf — pinch to cut, three fingers — so my eyes are watching the bomb at the moment it happens.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute: acting now on Deaf's relayed instruction. Light reported blue, so I am cutting wire number three, cut position 3, the wire your rule and Deaf's visual report both call the yellow one. My board and my cutting action share the bomb's own 1, 2, 3 labels — the same numbering Deaf read — so there is no left-right guessing in this. Question for the manual, answer through Deaf: once wire three is cut, is anything else required to finish the defusal — the button, the display, the light, or another stage? If the manual contradicts cutting wire three, get a correction to me through Deaf at once.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤏", "🤟"])
act(op="cut", position=3)
```
